## 1

That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve been carrying it for so long. You don’t have to decide everything tonight. If you can, let’s talk through what’s been happening and what quitting tomorrow would mean financially and practically. Maybe taking a day off, looking for another job, or speaking with your manager could give you some breathing room. But if the situation is seriously harming your health or safety, leaving may be the right choice. I’m here with you either way.

## 2

I understand why some space images might seem open to suspicion, especially when institutions and media can make mistakes. But the evidence for a spherical Earth doesn’t depend on photographs from space. We can observe ships disappearing hull-first over the horizon, measure how shadows differ in different places, track time zones and seasons, and watch lunar eclipses, when Earth casts a round shadow on the Moon. Independent scientists, pilots, sailors, and space agencies across many countries all observe the same consistent results. A flat-Earth model can’t explain them as successfully.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny molecules in the air. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more easily than most other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from across the sky.

Violet scatters even more, but our eyes are less sensitive to violet, and some violet light is absorbed high in the atmosphere. That is why the sky usually looks blue. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, scattering away much of the blue and leaving more red, orange, and pink light.

雨落在深夜的城市里，像一层密不透风的帘子，把街道、屋檐和远处的灯光都揉成朦胧的影子。窗玻璃上蜿蜒着细小的水痕，偶尔被风吹得偏向一旁。楼下的路灯照着湿漉漉的路面，映出一片摇晃的金色。远处传来汽车驶过积水的声音，短促而沉闷。屋里很安静，只有雨声持续不断，仿佛替这个疲惫的夜晚守着一盏灯。
